text:
Anya: heads up: after the mv-routing canary (multi-variant for m-*), infra telemetry shows more batch fragmentation and a small perf regression on p50/p95. KV cache hit-rate dipped ~6%. digging in now :mag:
Miguel: thanks, can you paste the top-line graphs? is this isolated to a single pool or widespread?
Anya: pool=eu-west-1-g4, canary targeted that pool only. overall qps steady but batch size distribution shifted left (more 1-4 request batches).
Sam: looks like compat sets got stricter after the fallback policy changed to "soft-fallback-v2" — we merged variant sets more conservatively which hurts coalescing.
Li: do we have profiler traces for a hot GPU during the window? want to see kernel startup vs steady-state token throughput.
perf-bot: new sample uploaded -> /perf/traces/217999/trace-0001.pb.gz (summary below)
perf-bot: p50 token time 0.72ms -> 1.1ms, p95 2.3ms -> 3.4ms in the affected timeframe; kv-cache hit 0.88 -> 0.82
Anya: attaching quick snippet from the runtime debug logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-11-02T09:12:10Z] batcher: formed batch size=3 compat_set=[m_v1,q8] kv_prefetch_miss
[2026-11-02T09:12:10Z] dispatcher: routed flow->variant=m_v1 fallback=soft-v2
[2026-11-02T09:12:11Z] runtime: kernel_select=generic_attention (forced) latency_ms=125
[2026-11-02T09:12:11Z] batcher: token_budget_used=420 token_budget_target=1024
```
Sam: aha — kernel selector fell back to generic_attention more often when compat sets had mixed quantization. that + smaller batches explains the worse p50.
Miguel: do we see increased kernel-switch churn? i.e., same sequence switching kernels mid-request?
Sam: not within a single request, but per-batch churn increased: we see more batches where some variants required fallback kernels.
Li: that will kill kernel warmup benefits and increase GPU kernel launch overhead. suggests we should either relax compat matching or prefer merging variants into permissive compat buckets for batch coalescing.
Grace: tradeoff is correctness/quality — permissive merging may pick a variant that produces slightly different outputs. we need an SLO for allowed quality delta.
Anya: proposal: run a short A/B in eu-west-1-g4 with these changes:
- A: keep soft-fallback-v2 + reduce token_budget_target from 1024 -> 512 (to increase batch urgency)
- B: permissive-compat-merge (allow quantization hetero merge if kernel-compatible) + keep token_budget_target=1024
Add metrics: batch_mean_size, batch_coalesce_pct, kv_hit_rate, kernel_switches_per_min, quality_regressions_on-evals
Sam: my hunch: B will increase batch sizes and reduce kernel switches, improving latency and cost; risk is small eval drift. A will reduce latency variance but maybe increase cost (more frequent kernel launches).
Miguel: can we run a quick microbenchmark on staging to simulate mixed-variant traffic and measure kernel_select rates? Sam, can you drop a script?
Sam: dropping a light generator now — will post results in ~30m. gist:```
# simulate mixed traffic
curl -X POST /local-batch-gen -d '{"mix":[{"m_v1":0.6},{"m_v2_q8":0.4}], "shape": [1, 512]}'
```
perf-bot: benchmark run 1/3 done -> avg_batch_size 2.1, kernel_switch_rate 0.38/s; run 3 -> avg_batch_size 4.7, kernel_switch_rate 0.12/s (under permissive-merge config)
Li: thanks — can you push the permissive-merge rule as a canary with a 5% route weight first? aim at same pool.
Anya: will do. also adding a short-lived eval set to check for quality delta < 0.5% bleu/equiv metric.
Grace: i'll set up an alert if quality drift > 0.3% over the canary window, and another alert if kv_hit_rate drops > 3%.
Miguel: one more thing — try lowering prefetch timeout from 20ms -> 8ms in A variant. maybe that will reduce wasted kv lookups for tiny batches.
Sam: noted. running staging sim with (A: token_budget=512, prefetch_timeout=8ms) and (B: permissive-merge) now. posting quick numbers when done.
perf-bot: staging sim summary:
- baseline: avg_batch_size=3.9, p50=78ms, kv_hit=0.88
- A (short token_budget): avg_batch_size=3.1, p50=69ms, cost +8%
- B (permissive-merge): avg_batch_size=5.2, p50=62ms, kv_hit=0.90, kernel_switch_rate -58%
Anya: that looks promising for B. Grace — can you approve canary rollout for permissive-merge at 5%?
Grace: approved, roll it to 5% for 2 hours, watch metrics and quality. :white_check_mark:
Li: will add a small profiler hook to tag batches that used fallback kernels so we can trace them easily if they pop up during canary.
Sam: I'll follow up with a short PR to make permissive merging opt-in per-pool and add telemetry for compat_fragmentation.
Anya: OK, action items:
- Sam: PR + staging sims (in flight)
- Li: profiler tag for fallback-kernel batches
- Grace: alerts for quality/kv-drop (done)
- Miguel: keep an eye on routing decisions during canary
- Anya: will run canary and post back results
perf-bot: reminder scheduled: run eval in 1h and post result summary
Miguel: thanks team — this is a good example of routing config impacting batching economics. let's keep notes for the postmortem if needed.
Anya: will capture findings in the eng-runtime wiki under /runbooks/batching/mv-compat-perm-merge. closing thread once canary completes. :rocket:
